title: UK Regulatory Monitor
subtitle: FCA · PRA · ICO · CMA · FRC — enforcement, guidance, and rulemaking
schedule_note: Updated every 6 hours via GitHub Actions

items.title: Consumers warned about misleading car finance 'money tips' claims ads
items.summary: Consumers are being warned to be wary of misleading car finance 'money tips' adverts issued by claims management companies (CMCs) and law firms on social media.

items.title: FCA secures confiscation order against Ponzi scheme fraudster
items.summary:
The FCA has secured a confiscation order of £452,286.80 against convicted fraudster Daniel Pugh.

Mr Pugh, 36, is serving a 7 years and 6 months prison sentence for defrauding investors out of £1.3m.

items.title: FCA consults on proposals to support strong, consistent standards in the SIPP market
items.summary: The FCA has set out plans to drive greater consistency of standards in self-invested pensions (SIPPs), while maintaining the flexibility and broad investment choice they offer.

items.title: The Bank, FCA and HM Treasury joint statement on Frontier AI models and cyber resilience
items.summary: Statement from the Bank of England, Financial Conduct Authority and HM Treasury

items.title: PRA fines The Bank of London and its parent company Oplyse Holdings Limited £2m for failing to act with integrity and misleading the PRA over their capital position
items.summary: The Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) has fined The Bank of London Group Limited and Oplyse Holdings Limited (formerly The Bank of London Group Holdings Limited)  £2 million for misleading the PRA over their capital positions, failing to act with

items.title: PRA publishes liquidity reform proposals
items.summary: The Prudential Regulation Authority has today published proposals aimed at ensuring banks can monetise liquid assets quickly in a fast-paced stress event – such as the collapse of Silicon Valley Bank in 2023.

items.title: PRA sets out adjustments to its market risk internal model approach under Basel 3.1
items.summary: The Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) has today published a consultation on the internal model approach to market risk (IMA), which represents the final piece of Basel 3.1’s implementation in the UK.

items.title: FCA proposes changes to help more people access mortgages
items.summary: First-time buyers, older borrowers and the self-employed could find it easier to get a mortgage, as the FCA sets out next steps to help reform the market.

items.title: Beyond the headlines: the unseen fight against financial crime
items.summary:
Speech by Therese Chambers, joint executive director of enforcement and market oversight, delivered at the International Bar Association (IBA) Anti-Corruption Conference.

I’ve been practising law for over 3 decades now.

items.title: FCA and Bank of England set out shared vision for tokenisation in UK wholesale markets
items.summary: The Financial Conduct Authority and the Bank of England set out a shared vision and seek industry views on the future of UK wholesale markets

items.title: PRA announces ring-fence change to reduce costs
items.summary: The Prudential Regulation Authority has today announced plans to consult on reforming rules around shared operational services for ring-fenced banks.

items.title: Bank of England streamlines reporting and disclosure requirements for bank failure regime
items.summary: The Bank of England and Prudential Regulation Authority have finalised a package of changes to firms’ resolution reporting and disclosure requirements which reduces the burden of regulation while maintaining a robust and credible regime that supports

items.title: Investors get real-time view of UK bond market activity for the first time
items.summary: For the first time, investors and market participants can access a single, real-time source of prices and trading activity across the UK bond market, following the launch of its bond consolidated tape, operated by ETS Connect UK.

items.title: FCA closes investigation into Drax Group PLC
items.summary: Drax Group PLC (Drax) has announced the FCA has closed its investigation into the company.We undertook an extensive investigation following concerns raised regarding disclosures to the market about the sustainability of Drax’s Canadian biomass.

items.title: PRA publishes plans to support resilience in the life insurance industry
items.summary: Funded reinsurance transactions involving UK life insurers will face enhanced regulatory requirements under new proposals unveiled today by the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA).

items.title: Court endorses CMA action as Emma Sleep agrees to change sales practices
items.summary: The CMA has secured a court-endorsed settlement from mattress firm Emma Sleep after concerns its sales practices misled consumers.

items.title: CMA orders Marks Electrical to refund customers over pre-selected extra charges
items.summary: Marks Electrical must refund nearly 40,000 customers and pay a fine after it automatically opted customers into additional paid services.

items.title: Bank of England launches policy statement and draft rules on regulating systemic stablecoins
items.summary: The Bank of England has today published its policy statement and draft Code of Practice (rules) for systemic stablecoin issuers.

items.title: Bank of England and Financial Conduct Authority – Memorandum of Understanding on the supervision of Financial Market Infrastructure
items.summary: Joint statement from the Bank of England and Financial Conduct Authority

items.title: CMA response to government in relation to childcare provision
items.summary: A letter from Sarah Cardell, Chief Executive of the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA), to Bridget Phillipson, Secretary of State for Education.

items.title: CMA advice to Defra on reform of the Veterinary Surgeons Act 1966
items.summary: The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) has published its advice to Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (Defra) on the reform of veterinary sector regulation.

items.title: Later life lending: building the fourth retirement pillar
items.summary:
Speech by Emad Aladhal, director of retail banking at the Later Life Lending Summit.

IntroductionIn the years ahead, housing wealth will become an increasing part of how many people provide for their retirement.

items.title: FCA decides to fine Carlos Ricardo Fuenmayor £99,600 for disclosure failures
items.summary: FCA decides to fine Carlos Ricardo Fuenmayor £99,600 for disclosure failures

items.title: AI in financial services: shaping our approach through industry engagement
items.summary: Firms are using AI to drive efficiency, support decision-making and deliver better outcomes for consumers and markets. We want to support that innovation. But it must be safe, responsible and well governed.

items.title: Silicon Marketing Limited in administration
items.summary: On 21 May 2026, Silicon Marketing Limited (Silicon) entered administration. Carrie James and Nick Parsk of Oury Clark were appointed as joint administrators.

items.title: Bank of England and FCA MoU on supervision of market infrastructure: 2025/26 review
items.summary:
The Bank of England has published a joint review with the FCA on how the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for financial market infrastructure (FMI) is working.

The Bank of England and the FCA (the authorities) cooperate on the supervision of FMIs.

items.title: FCA and PRA confirm changes to streamline senior manager accountability and boost growth
items.summary: The PRA and FCA have set out reforms to the Senior Managers and Certification Regime, designed to reduce costs and offer greater flexibility.

items.title: Tribunal was “wrong” to reject CMA phenytoin decision, says Court
items.summary: The Court of Appeal has ruled the Tribunal was “wrong to set aside the [CMA’s] decision” in relation to its investigation into phenytoin – a life-saving epilepsy drug.

items.title: Next steps for veterinary services for household pets: what the CMA's remedies mean in practice
items.summary: A speech by Martin Coleman, Non-Executive Director and Panel Chair, delivered at BVA Live 2026.

items.title: Opening the door to mortgages: rules focused on better outcomes for people
items.summary: Buying a home is different now to even a decade ago.People are living longer, the way they work has changed and, for many, how much they earn can vary month-to-month.
